A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

TRO induces a profound cellular acidity as a result of NHE1 inhibition which in turn activates EGFR/MEKK/ERK pathway and this signaling cascade is responsible for the growth arrest of MCF-7 breast cancer derived cells.
TRO induces a profound cellular pH reduction and growth inhibition of breast cancer-derived MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231 cells via NHE1-inhibited acid extrusion.
TRO-induced growth-arrest in MCF-10A cells is dependent upon the EGFR pathway and that in MCF- 7 cells is dependent upon NHE1-mediated acid extrudion and cellular acidosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

troglitazoine, a drug that was withdrawn from the market because of hepatotoxicity, has anti-proliferative activity that is independent of the hepatotoxicity and is mediated through inhibition of the NHE1 transporter.
the TRO-activated EGFR pathway and TRO-inhibition of the NHE1-mediated acid extrudion pathway both play a role in the TRO-mediated growth arrest of breast cancer derived MFC-7 cells.
troglitazoine, a PPAR gamma agonist, inhibits NHE1 and induces a cellular acidosis in breast cancer derived cells.
